properties.name: The handshake writes down who connected and what they agreed to speak
properties.rationale:
Anthony's word 2026-08-28, choosing this over asking the reporter to wrap his MCP command with a tee script.

⭐ THE DESIGN CONSTRAINT IS THE WHOLE POINT: THE ANSWER MUST BE READABLE WHEN THE PROTOCOL IS NOT WORKING. This exists because of `fact:the-signpost-instructs-a-party-that-cannot-act-and-the-absent-client-was-named` — a client that reads only `content` gets a stub from every structured tool, so the question "why can I not read anything?" CANNOT be answered through a tool reply. It has to reach disk. That is why this is a sidecar and not a field on `graph_report.served_by`, which is exactly the reply such a client cannot read.

WHY IT ANSWERS THE RIGHT QUESTION. `structuredContent` arrived in MCP `2025-06-18`, and rmcp still negotiates `2024-11-05` and `2025-03-26`. If a reporting client requested a revision that PREDATES the field, version-gating is the spec-sanctioned fix. If it requested a modern one and still reads only `content`, that is a conformance gap and version-gating would do nothing. Those need different remedies and nothing could tell them apart.

⚠️ IT RECORDS WHAT THE REVISION CONTAINS, NEVER WHAT THE CLIENT READS. The derived field is named `protocol_has_structured_content`, not `supports_structured_content`, and carries a note saying so. The distinction is the entire subject of this investigation: a negotiated version is what a client CLAIMS to speak, not proof of what it implemented. A flattering name here would be the same overreach `fact:a-findings-name-can-claim-more-than-its-data-...` describes, committed while fixing its cousin.

⚠️ THE COUPLING THIS ACCEPTS, NAMED BEFORE IT IS TAKEN. `negotiate_protocol_version` is `pub(crate)` in rmcp, so overriding `initialize` means MIRRORING a four-line rule this crate cannot call: echo the client's version if `supported_protocol_versions()` contains it, else the server's fallback. A test pins the rule, following the precedent set by the test that pins which version `ProtocolVersion::LATEST` resolves to — this project already refuses to let an rmcp move happen silently.

NO TIMESTAMP INSIDE THE FILE. It is overwritten on every handshake, so it always describes the CURRENT connection, and the file's own mtime says when. Inventing a clock for a field a reader can get from the filesystem would add a dependency and a thing to be wrong about.
properties.subject: system
properties.summary: reflow2 overrides `ServerHandler::initialize` to record the client's self-reported name and version, the protocol revision it REQUESTED, the revision negotiated, and what this server offers — written to `<graph>.client.json` beside the store, alongside the existing `.meta.json` and `.server.json` sidecars. Answers "which client am I and what did we agree on?" for every future field report, without the reporter instrumenting their own machine.
